claim_text: Reducing dietary sodium intake lowers blood pressure in adults, with a dose-response pattern and heterogeneous effect magnitude across populations.
applicability: population-level prevention/risk-factor context; not individualized treatment advice
uncertainty: effect size varies by baseline BP, age and population
prohibited_overclaims: this dish causes hypertension; any single dish predicts cardiovascular risk; lower sodium is always better for every clinical patient

claim_text: WHO recommends reducing sodium intake and recommends less than 2 g/day sodium in adults to reduce blood pressure and cardiovascular risk.
applicability: daily intake recommendation; selected clinical conditions may require supervised diets
uncertainty: dish-level compliance cannot be computed while serving/nutrition basis is unresolved
prohibited_overclaims: classify a dish as safe/unsafe for hypertension from unresolved-basis sodium values

claim_text: Increasing potassium intake within appropriate ranges can lower blood pressure, with stronger effects in people with hypertension and at higher sodium intake; the dose-response is not simply linear.
population: adults; evidence especially informative in hypertension
applicability: population-level dietary context; not a recommendation for unrestricted potassium supplementation
uncertainty: high-intake/supplementation effects are less certain and may differ in treated subgroups
prohibited_overclaims: more potassium is always better; food potassium equals unrestricted supplementation; suitable for every kidney/medication context

claim_text: Higher dietary fibre intake is associated with lower risks of several major noncommunicable disease outcomes, with complementary randomized-trial evidence for improvements in selected risk factors.
uncertainty: major long-term disease outcomes are supported substantially by observational evidence; disease-specific causality should not be overclaimed
prohibited_overclaims: a single high-fibre dish prevents cancer/diabetes; direct therapeutic claim for a diagnosed patient

claim_text: WHO recommends that adults consume at least 25 g/day of naturally occurring dietary fibre as part of a healthy carbohydrate pattern.
applicability: daily dietary target, not a dish-level threshold
uncertainty: cannot calculate contribution to daily target until dish nutrition basis and serving semantics are confirmed
prohibited_overclaims: label a dish as meeting/failing daily fibre guidance using unresolved denominator

claim_text: Reducing saturated fat intake for at least two years can reduce combined cardiovascular events, while effects on all-cause and cardiovascular mortality are less clear.
population: adults with or without cardiovascular disease in long-term trials
applicability: long-term dietary pattern; not a single-meal causal effect
uncertainty: individual endpoints and mortality effects are less certain; replacement nutrient context matters
prohibited_overclaims: SFA reduction necessarily lowers mortality; a single dish determines cardiovascular outcome

claim_text: WHO recommends that saturated fat provide no more than 10% of total energy, with replacement by unsaturated fats or carbohydrate from naturally fibre-rich foods.
population: people aged 2 years and older for the main guidance
uncertainty: dish-level grams cannot establish percent-energy compliance while denominator is unresolved
prohibited_overclaims: classify a dish as guideline-compliant from SFA grams alone
